# Setting Up the Film Development Workflow

The Film Development workflow tracks every roll of film through your lab — from the parcel arriving, through twin checking, developing and scanning, to the finished job — with due dates, customer updates and exception handling built in. Your team works from the **Film Development App** on tablets or phones at the bench, while OrderHub remains your control centre.

This page is the overview: it walks the setup in order and points to the detailed article for each area.

---

## Before you start

Two things need to be true first:

1. **Your film categories are mapped to a production process.** The workflow decides "is this job film?" from the job's category and your process mapping — an unmapped category is invisible to film development. See *Assigning Pixfizz Categories to Production Processes*.
2. **You know which stages your lab actually runs.** Twin checking is always part of the workflow — it's where each roll gets its identity. Receiving, developing and scanning are each optional, and any combination works: a lab can run everything, or twin checking alone.

---

## Step 1 — Switch on Film Development

Go to **Settings** > **Organization** > **Film Development** > **General** and set the workflow to **Film Development**. This hides the legacy Film Scans page; from now on, uploaded roll folders are matched to jobs automatically by their twin-check code.

![Switch on Film Development](https://nazkcvruighrhpgcarxg.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/help-documentation-images/4abd8355-b615-4d37-830c-0ee400af0430.png)

---

## Step 2 — Choose your stages

On the same **General** tab, the **Stages** section lists **Receive (order book-in)**, **Develop** and **Scan**, each with its own switch. Turn on the stages your lab runs — rolls flow through the active stages in order and skip the rest. Each stage row also holds its **Send notifications** settings, so you can message customers as their film clears a stage (for example "your film has been developed").

If you only want to be asked about film that's actually in transit — mail-in and drop-box orders rather than film handed over in store — see the expected-orders setting in the Receive article.

---

## Step 3 — Set up Twin Checking

On the **Twin Checking** tab, switch on **Twin Checking** and review:

*   **Allowed job statuses for lookup** and **Allowed processes for lookup** — which jobs can be twin-checked (typically New and in_production, and your film process).
*   **Camera scanning** — lets operators read pre-printed twin-check labels with a camera instead of typing.
*   **Record film stock** — operators can record which film stock each roll is, by scanning the barcode on the canister.
*   **"No scanning required" option mapping** — marks develop-only orders automatically from your storefront options. See *Develop-Only Film (No Scanning)*.

---

## Step 4 — Timings and due dates (optional)

On the **Timings** tab, switch on **Work out film due dates from these timings** to have OrderHub set film due dates from your real working hours: set your **Working days**, when the **Day starts** and **finishes**, and the **Hours each stage takes**. The clock starts when you book the order in (or at the first twin check if you don't book in), and always promises the end of a working day. Develop-only film is automatically promised sooner, and print jobs created from scans get their own **Print (after scanning)** hours.

---

## Step 5 — Scanning exceptions (optional)

On the **Scanning Exceptions** tab, set up the problems your lab records against rolls — blank roll, wet film, wrong process and so on. Each exception type has a behaviour (**Just record it**, **Ends the roll**, or **Needs a decision**) and can **Offer to message the customer** with your own email or text wording when it's recorded.

---

## Step 6 — Completion settings

Back on the **General** tab, two switches decide how film jobs finish themselves:

*   **Auto-complete film jobs when all rolls are uploaded** — the job completes when every roll's scans have arrived (or, for develop-only work, when developing is done).
*   **When every roll on a job ends with an exception** — choose whether a job whose rolls all ended (blank, damaged…) is left open, completed, or cancelled.

---

## Step 7 — The Film Development App

Your team signs into the **Film Development App** at **film.pixfizz.com** on a tablet or phone at the bench. Home shows each stage's queue, today's intake, priorities and flags; operators book in parcels, assign twin checks with the camera, and mark rolls done at each stage. Everything they do updates OrderHub live.

![Film Development App](https://nazkcvruighrhpgcarxg.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/help-documentation-images/ca56b25a-1a06-42ff-99a4-8eec9c72b7b1.png)

---

## Day to day

Once set up, the daily rhythm is: **book in** what arrives → **twin check** each roll → **develop** → **scan** → files upload and jobs complete themselves. The app's **Metrics** screen answers "are we keeping up, are we keeping promises, where's the pile-up", and the **Intake** board tracks each day's film as a batch until every roll is finished.

---

## Good to know

*   Every stage beyond twin checking is optional — start small (twin checking only) and switch stages on as your team is ready.
*   Settings changes never rewrite history: due dates already set stay put, and existing jobs are never re-flagged by new mappings.
*   Customer messages are always off by default — nothing emails or texts a customer until you switch it on and write the wording.
